chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a woman upon whom dawn rises while she is menstruating in the month of Ramadan,
then when morning came she became pure, and she had already eaten; then she performed the ẓuhr and ʿaṣr prayers. What should she do regarding that day in which she became pure?
He عليه السلام said: “She should abstain in fasting, but it is not counted for her.”

key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, the start time relevant to the validity of the fast
key_terms.تَصُومُ: she observes fasting abstention for the remainder of the day
key_terms.حَائِضٌ: a menstruating woman, one in a state preventing fasting and prayer
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, during which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.صَلَّتِ الظُّهْرَ وَالْعَصْرَ: she performed the noon and afternoon prayers after becoming pure
key_terms.وَلَا تَعْتَدُّ بِهِ: it is not counted as a valid fast for that day

ai.seo_question: If a woman becomes pure from menstruation after dawn in Ramadan, does that day count as a fast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a menstruating woman in Ramadan who becomes pure after dawn. She is to observe abstention for the rest of the day, but that day does not count as a valid fast. It relates to the rulings of fasting, ritual purity, and women's legal duties in worship.
